pr_title: types: convert string to MySQL BIT correctly
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #18681 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

`LOAD DATA` does not take effect on BIT. Because `LOAD DATA` regards all input as strings and TiDB cannot convert any string to bit correctly

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

- convert string to bit correctly
- consider `true`, `false`, `0`, `1`

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

issue_context.title: load data can't load value 0/1/true/false for bit(1)
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

1. Create data file `test.txt`
```
cat test.txt
true    false   0       1
```
2. Start a tidb and connect.
```
use test;
create table t(a bit(1),b bit(1),c bit(1),d bit(1));
load data local infile 'test.txt' into table t fields terminated by '\t' enclosed by '^' lines terminated by '\n';
select * from t;
+------+------+------+------+
| a    | b    | c    | d    |
+------+------+------+------+
| NULL | NULL | NULL | NULL |
+------+------+------+------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

```



### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

Can load successfully.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

Null.

### 4. Affected version (Required)

<!-- v3.0.0, v4.0.0, etc -->
All version.

### 5. Root Cause Analysis

<!-- should be filled by the investigator before it's closed -->

String '0','1','true','false' convert bit(1) will cause truncated.
comments:
`LOAD DATA` regards all input as strings and [`(d *Datum) convertToMysqlBit(sc *stmtctx.StatementContext, target *FieldType)`](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/51dc39308885a0523af9927f364845518ebfcb82/types/datum.go#L1347) cannot convert any string to bit correctly, so it's always `NULL` value. There are two options to work around this:
 - make some changes to support it
 - recommend users to use `SET` clause to convert string to base-10 integer

`load data local infile 'test.txt' into table t (@val1, @val2, @val3, @val4) set c1 = if(@val1='true', 1, 0)...`

> [MySQL Manually](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/load-data.html)
BIT values cannot be loaded directly using binary notation (for example, b'011010'). To work around this, use the SET clause to strip off the leading b' and trailing ' and perform a base-2 to base-10 conversion so that MySQL loads the values into the BIT column properly:

review_comments:
This sentence of SQL has nothing to do with convert. It can be seen from the following that these values can be converted correctly, but they are returned as binary, so the output to MySQL Client may not be displayed.
```sql
MySQL [test]> select true, HEX(b'1'), HEX(cast(true as binary));
+------+-----------+---------------------------+
| TRUE | HEX(b'1') | HEX(cast(true as binary)) |
+------+-----------+---------------------------+
|    1 | 01        | 31                        |
+------+-----------+---------------------------+
1 row in set (0.001 sec)

MySQL [test]> select true, b'1', cast(true as binary);
+------+------+----------------------+
| TRUE | b'1' | cast(true as binary) |
+------+------+----------------------+
|    1 |     | 1                    |
+------+------+----------------------+
1 row in set (0.001 sec)
```
I think these are two different problems, and it's best to solve it in another PR
